question.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[6X+2].$

$$
f(x)=\frac{4}{{x}^{5}},\,x\ge 1
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we simplify using the properties of expected value:

$$
\text{E}[6X+2]=6\text{E}[X]+2
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

$$
\text{E}[X]={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we calculate the expected value of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }x\cdot \frac{4}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{4}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={-\frac{4}{3{x}^{3}}|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[6X+2] & =6\text{E}[X]+2 \\  & =6\cdot \frac{4}{3}+2 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$
